name: Chaos
title: The First Void
description: The yawning void that existed before all else, from which the first primordial gods emerged.

name: Gaia
title: Mother Earth
description: The primeval goddess who personifies the Earth itself, mother and grandmother to nearly every god that followed her.

name: Uranus
title: Father Sky
description: The primordial sky god, son and husband of Gaia, whose union with her produced the Titans before he was overthrown by his son Cronus.

name: Nyx
title: Goddess of Night
description: The primordial goddess of night, so ancient and powerful that even Zeus is said to fear her.

name: Erebus
title: God of Darkness
description: The primordial personification of deep darkness and shadow, consort of Nyx and father of Aether and Hemera.

name: Pontus
title: The Sea
description: The primordial personification of the sea, born of Gaia alone, father of the earliest sea gods.

name: Aether
title: God of Light
description: The primordial personification of the bright upper air breathed by the gods, son of Nyx and Erebus.

name: Hemera
title: Goddess of Day
description: The primordial personification of day, who alternates with her mother Nyx in ruling the passage of light and dark.

name: Cronus
title: King of the Titans
description: The youngest of the first Titans, he overthrew his father Uranus and ruled during the mythic Golden Age, before being overthrown in turn by his son Zeus.

name: Rhea
title: Mother of the Gods
description: Titaness of fertility and motherhood, wife of Cronus, who saved the infant Zeus from being devoured by tricking her husband with a swaddled stone.

name: Oceanus
title: The World-Ocean
description: The Titan who personifies the great river believed to encircle the entire world, father of the three thousand river gods and Oceanid nymphs.

name: Tethys
title: Titaness of Fresh Water
description: Titaness of fresh water, wife of Oceanus and mother of the rivers and the Oceanid nymphs.

name: Hyperion
title: Titan of Light
description: The Titan of heavenly light, father of the sun, moon, and dawn through his children Helios, Selene, and Eos.

name: Theia
title: Titaness of Sight
description: Titaness associated with sight and shining light, wife of Hyperion and mother of Helios, Selene, and Eos.

name: Mnemosyne
title: Titaness of Memory
description: Titaness who personifies memory, and mother of the nine Muses by Zeus.

name: Themis
title: Titaness of Divine Law
description: Titaness of divine law and order, who presides over prophecy and custom, and later gives counsel to Zeus on Olympus.

name: Iapetus
title: Titan of Mortality
description: Titan associated with mortal lifespan and craftsmanship, father of Atlas, Prometheus, and Epimetheus.

name: Crius
title: Titan of the South
description: One of the lesser-chronicled Titans, associated with the constellations and the turning of the seasons.

name: Coeus
title: Titan of Intellect
description: Titan of intelligent inquiry, father of Leto by Phoebe, and grandfather of Apollo and Artemis.

name: Phoebe
title: Titaness of Prophecy
description: Titaness of prophecy who held the Oracle of Delphi before passing it down to her grandson Apollo.

name: Atlas
title: The Sky-Bearer
description: A second-generation Titan condemned by Zeus to hold up the heavens on his shoulders for eternity after the Titans' defeat.

name: Prometheus
title: The Fire-Bringer
description: A cunning Titan who defied Zeus by stealing fire and giving it to humanity, for which he was chained to a rock to have his liver eternally devoured by an eagle.

name: Epimetheus
title: Titan of Afterthought
description: Brother of Prometheus, whose ill-considered acceptance of Pandora as a gift from the gods brought suffering into the world.

name: Zeus
title: King of the Gods
description: Youngest son of Cronus and Rhea, he overthrew the Titans and rules Olympus as king of gods and men.

name: Hera
title: Queen of the Gods
description: Queen of Olympus and goddess of marriage and family, wife and sister of Zeus, often provoked to jealousy by his many affairs.

name: Poseidon
title: God of the Sea
description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses, brother of Zeus, known for his volatile temper and his rivalry with Athena over the city of Athens.

name: Demeter
title: Goddess of the Harvest
description: Goddess of grain and the harvest, whose grief over her daughter Persephone's abduction to the underworld created the cycle of the seasons.

name: Athena
title: Goddess of Wisdom
description: Goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare, born fully armored from the head of Zeus, and patron of the city of Athens.

name: Apollo
title: God of the Sun and Prophecy
description: God of music, prophecy, healing, and light, twin brother of Artemis, who speaks to mortals through the Oracle of Delphi.

name: Artemis
title: Goddess of the Hunt
description: Goddess of the hunt, wilderness, and the moon, twin sister of Apollo, fiercely protective of her chastity and of wild creatures.

name: Ares
title: God of War
description: God of the brutal, chaotic aspects of war, disliked by most other gods but a favored lover of Aphrodite.

name: Aphrodite
title: Goddess of Love
description: Goddess of love, beauty, and desire, said to have been born from sea foam, whose favor in the Judgment of Paris helped ignite the Trojan War.

name: Hephaestus
title: God of the Forge
description: The lame god of fire and the forge, master craftsman of the Olympians, husband of Aphrodite despite their mismatched marriage.

name: Hermes
title: Messenger of the Gods
description: Swift messenger of the gods and guide of souls to the underworld, patron of travelers, merchants, and thieves alike.

name: Dionysus
title: God of Wine
description: God of wine, festivity, and theatrical ecstasy, the youngest Olympian, born from Zeus's thigh after his mortal mother Semele perished.

name: Hades
title: Lord of the Underworld
description: God of the dead and ruler of the underworld, brother of Zeus and Poseidon, feared but not evil, presiding fairly over the realm of the dead.

name: Hestia
title: Goddess of the Hearth
description: Gentle goddess of the hearth and domestic life, eldest of the Olympian siblings, who gave up her throne on Olympus to keep the peace.

name: Persephone
title: Queen of the Underworld
description: Daughter of Zeus and Demeter, abducted by Hades to be his queen; her seasonal return to the surface world governs spring and winter.

name: Eros
title: God of Love
description: Winged god of love and desire, son of Aphrodite and Ares, whose arrows spark irresistible passion in gods and mortals alike.

name: Nike
title: Goddess of Victory
description: Winged goddess of victory in war and athletic competition, a close attendant of Zeus and Athena.

name: Iris
title: Goddess of the Rainbow
description: Goddess of the rainbow and personal messenger of Hera, said to travel between heaven, earth, and the sea.

name: Hecate
title: Goddess of Magic
description: Goddess of magic, crossroads, and necromancy, who alone among the older gods retained great honor from Zeus.

name: Pan
title: God of the Wild
description: Goat-legged god of the wild, shepherds, and rustic music, whose sudden appearance could inspire the terror that gave us the word 'panic'.

name: Nemesis
title: Goddess of Retribution
description: Goddess who deals out retribution against those guilty of hubris, restoring balance to fortune's excess.

name: Hypnos
title: God of Sleep
description: Gentle god of sleep who lives in a dark cave in the underworld, twin brother of Thanatos.

name: Thanatos
title: God of Death
description: The personification of peaceful death, twin brother of Hypnos, distinct from the violent death dealt in war.

name: Helios
title: God of the Sun
description: God who drives the sun in a golden chariot across the sky each day, seeing and hearing all that happens on earth.

name: Selene
title: Goddess of the Moon
description: Goddess who drives the moon across the night sky, sister of Helios and Eos.

name: Eos
title: Goddess of the Dawn
description: Goddess of the dawn, who opens the gates of heaven each morning for her brother Helios to begin his journey.

name: Asclepius
title: God of Medicine
description: Son of Apollo and a legendary physician deified for his healing skill, so effective he could raise the dead.

name: Eris
title: Goddess of Discord
description: Goddess of discord and strife, whose golden apple inscribed 'to the fairest' set off the Judgment of Paris and, ultimately, the Trojan War.

name: Morpheus
title: God of Dreams
description: Son of Hypnos and the most skilled of the dream spirits, able to take any human form to appear in mortals' dreams.

name: The Moirai
title: The Fates
description: The three sister goddesses of destiny who spin, measure, and cut the thread of every mortal life, their decisions binding even for the gods.

name: The Muses
title: The Nine Muses
description: The nine daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne who inspire literature, science, and the arts.

name: The Graces
title: The Three Graces
description: Three goddesses of charm, beauty, and creativity who attend Aphrodite and bring joy to gods and mortals alike.

name: The Erinyes
title: The Furies
description: Ancient chthonic goddesses of vengeance who relentlessly punish those guilty of crimes such as murder and oath-breaking, especially against family.

name: Heracles
title: The Mightiest of Heroes
description: Son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene, famed for his superhuman strength and the Twelve Labors he performed as penance, eventually earning a place among the gods.

name: Perseus
title: Slayer of Medusa
description: Son of Zeus and Danaë, who beheaded the gorgon Medusa with the aid of the gods and later rescued Andromeda from a sea monster.

name: Theseus
title: Slayer of the Minotaur
description: Legendary king of Athens who ventured into the Labyrinth of Crete and slew the Minotaur with the help of Ariadne's thread.

name: Jason
title: Leader of the Argonauts
description: Leader of the Argonauts, who sailed the ship Argo on a quest to retrieve the Golden Fleece from Colchis.

name: Odysseus
title: The Wanderer of Ithaca
description: Cunning king of Ithaca whose ten-year journey home from the Trojan War, chronicled in the Odyssey, was filled with monsters, gods, and trials.

name: Achilles
title: Hero of the Trojan War
description: The greatest warrior of the Greeks at Troy, nearly invincible but for his famous heel, whose wrath drives the plot of the Iliad.

name: Ajax
title: The Great Defender
description: One of the mightiest Greek warriors at Troy, second only to Achilles in strength, who took his own life after losing a dispute over Achilles' armor.

name: Hector
title: Prince of Troy
description: The greatest warrior of Troy and its crown prince, who defended his city bravely before falling to Achilles.

name: Aeneas
title: The Trojan Survivor
description: A Trojan prince, son of Aphrodite, who escaped the fall of Troy and whose descendants were said to found Rome.

name: Atalanta
title: The Swift Huntress
description: A swift-footed heroine and huntress who joined the hunt for the Calydonian Boar and challenged suitors to footraces they could not win.

name: Bellerophon
title: Tamer of Pegasus
description: A hero who tamed the winged horse Pegasus and rode him into the sky to slay the monstrous Chimera.

name: Orpheus
title: The Divine Musician
description: A legendary musician whose songs could charm beasts and stones, famed for his doomed journey into the underworld to reclaim his wife Eurydice.

name: Oedipus
title: King of Thebes
description: Tragic king of Thebes who unknowingly fulfilled a prophecy to kill his father and marry his mother, and solved the riddle of the Sphinx.

name: Cadmus
title: Founder of Thebes
description: Legendary founder and first king of Thebes, who slew a dragon and sowed its teeth to raise an army of warriors from the earth.

name: Meleager
title: Hero of the Calydonian Hunt
description: Prince who led the hunt for the Calydonian Boar, his life magically tied to the burning of a log kept by his mother.

name: Paris
title: Prince of Troy
description: Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen, after being promised her love by Aphrodite in the Judgment of Paris, sparked the Trojan War.

name: Helen
title: Helen of Troy
description: The most beautiful woman in the world, wife of Menelaus of Sparta, whose elopement with Paris ignited the Trojan War.

name: Penelope
title: The Faithful Queen
description: Wife of Odysseus, who faithfully outwitted a hall of suitors during her husband's twenty-year absence, weaving and unweaving a burial shroud to delay them.

name: Medusa
title: The Gorgon
description: Once a beautiful maiden cursed by Athena into a monstrous gorgon with living snakes for hair, whose gaze turned onlookers to stone, until she was beheaded by Perseus.

name: Stheno
title: The Gorgon Sister
description: The eldest and fiercest of the three Gorgon sisters, immortal unlike Medusa.

name: Euryale
title: The Gorgon Sister
description: One of the immortal Gorgon sisters, known for her piercing, wailing cry.

name: Minotaur
title: The Bull of Crete
description: A monstrous being with the body of a man and the head of a bull, imprisoned within the Labyrinth of Crete and fed a tribute of youths until slain by Theseus.

name: Cerberus
title: Hound of the Underworld
description: The monstrous three-headed hound who guards the gates of the underworld, preventing the dead from leaving and the living from entering.

name: Hydra
title: The Lernaean Hydra
description: A many-headed serpent that regrew two heads for every one severed, ultimately destroyed by Heracles as one of his Twelve Labors.

name: Chimera
title: The Fire-Breathing Beast
description: A fire-breathing hybrid monster with the parts of a lion, goat, and serpent, slain by Bellerophon riding Pegasus.

name: Sphinx
title: The Riddling Sphinx
description: A winged monster with the body of a lion and the head of a woman, who terrorized Thebes with a deadly riddle until Oedipus solved it.

name: Polyphemus
title: The Cyclops
description: A one-eyed giant son of Poseidon, who trapped Odysseus and his crew in his cave before being blinded and outwitted by them.

name: The Sirens
title: The Sea Sirens
description: Bird-bodied maidens whose irresistible song lured sailors to wreck their ships upon the rocks.

name: Scylla
title: The Six-Headed Terror
description: A monstrous sea creature with six snapping heads who devours sailors passing through her narrow strait, opposite the whirlpool Charybdis.

name: Charybdis
title: The Great Whirlpool
description: A monstrous whirlpool that swallows the sea three times a day, posing a deadly hazard alongside Scylla in a narrow strait.

name: Pegasus
title: The Winged Horse
description: A divine winged horse born from Medusa's blood when she was slain, later tamed by Bellerophon.

name: Chiron
title: The Wise Centaur
description: A wise and gentle centaur, unlike his savage kin, who tutored many of Greece's greatest heroes in medicine, archery, and music.

name: The Harpies
title: The Snatchers
description: Winged spirits with the bodies of birds and faces of women, who swoop down to snatch away food and people as agents of divine punishment.

name: Nemean Lion
title: The Nemean Lion
description: A monstrous lion with an impenetrable golden hide, strangled barehanded by Heracles as the first of his Twelve Labors.

name: Python
title: The Serpent of Delphi
description: A monstrous serpent born of Gaia who guarded the oracle at Delphi until slain by the young god Apollo.

name: Ladon
title: The Guardian Dragon
description: A hundred-headed dragon who coils around the tree of golden apples in the Garden of the Hesperides, guarding it eternally.

name: Mount Olympus
title: Home of the Gods
description: The tallest mountain in Greece, believed to be the dwelling place of the twelve Olympian gods and the seat of Zeus's throne.

name: The Underworld
title: Realm of the Dead
description: The shadowy realm beneath the earth where the souls of the dead dwell, ruled over by Hades and Persephone.

name: Tartarus
title: The Abyss
description: A deep abyss far below the underworld used as a dungeon of torment for the wicked and the imprisoned Titans.

name: Elysium
title: The Blessed Fields
description: A paradise reserved in the underworld for heroes and the virtuous, where the souls of the blessed live in eternal ease.

name: River Styx
title: The River of the Underworld
description: The principal river of the underworld, across which the ferryman Charon carries the souls of the dead, and by which the gods swear their most binding oaths.

name: Troy
title: The Besieged City
description: A great city in Asia Minor besieged for ten years by the Greeks in the Trojan War, sparked by the abduction of Helen.

name: Crete
title: Island of the Labyrinth
description: A Mediterranean island ruled by King Minos, home to the Labyrinth that imprisoned the Minotaur.

name: Delphi
title: Seat of the Oracle
description: A sanctuary on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, home to the Oracle of Apollo, considered by the Greeks to be the center of the world.

name: Ithaca
title: Kingdom of Odysseus
description: A small island kingdom in western Greece, home of Odysseus and Penelope, and the destination of Odysseus's long journey home.

name: Thebes
title: The Seven-Gated City
description: A major city of ancient Greece founded by Cadmus, setting for the tragedies of Oedipus and his family.

name: Sparta
title: The Warrior City
description: A powerful city-state in the Peloponnese, home of Helen and Menelaus, renowned for its disciplined warriors.

name: Mycenae
title: City of Agamemnon
description: A fortified Bronze Age city, seat of King Agamemnon, who led the Greek forces in the Trojan War.

name: Athens
title: City of Athena
description: The great city of Attica, won by Athena in a contest against Poseidon and placed under her protection.

name: Colchis
title: Land of the Golden Fleece
description: A distant kingdom on the eastern shore of the Black Sea, home to the Golden Fleece sought by Jason and the Argonauts.
